Code (single file):

```python
import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import time
import random
import re
import json
from urllib.parse import urljoin

# -----------------------------
# Simple stopwords (for extractive summarization)
# -----------------------------
STOP_WORDS = {
    'the','and','a','an','of','in','to','with','for','on','at','by','from','that',
    'this','be','as','is','are','was','were','will','would','can','could','should',
    'has','have','had','it','its','they','them','we','you','your','yours','our','ours',
    'but','or','if','not','no','into','than','then','when','where','how','why','what',
    'which','who','i','they','them','these','those','am','being','do','did','done','so',
    'also','about','after','before','between','during','through','across','over','under',
    'above','below','inside','outside','again','more','most','some','any','other','such',
    'only'
}

# -----------------------------
# Utility: split text into sentences (naive but effective)
# -----------------------------
def split_sentences(text):
    # Simple sentence splitter based on punctuation
    parts = re.split(r'(?<=[.!?])\s+', text.strip())
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]

# -----------------------------
# Utility: tokenize words (lowercased, alphanumeric)
# -----------------------------
def tokenize(text):
    return re.findall(r'[a-zA-Z]+', text.lower())

# -----------------------------
# Extractive summarization (frequency-based)
# -----------------------------
def summarize_extractive(text, max_sentences=3):
    sentences = split_sentences(text)
    if len(sentences) <= max_sentences:
        return text  # Already short

    words = tokenize(text)
    # Build frequency map excluding stopwords
    freq = {}
    for w in words:
        if w in STOP_WORDS:
            continue
        freq[w] = freq.get(w, 0) + 1
    if not freq:
        # fallback: return first N sentences
        return ' '.join(sentences[:max_sentences])

    # Score each sentence by word frequency
    sentence_scores = []
    for i, sent in enumerate(sentences):
        sent_words = tokenize(sent)
        score = sum(freq.get(w, 0) for w in sent_words)
        sentence_scores.append((i, score, sent))

    # Pick top N sentences by score, then preserve original order
    top_n = sorted(sentence_scores, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:max_sentences]
    top_indices = sorted([idx for idx, _, _ in top_n])

    summary_sentences = [sentences[i] for i in top_indices]
    # If somehow none selected, fall back
    if not summary_sentences:
        summary_sentences = sentences[:max_sentences]

    return ' '.join(summary_sentences)

# -----------------------------
# Optional: Transformer-based summarization (requires transformers)
# -----------------------------
def summarize_transformer(text, max_length=130, model_name=None):
    try:
        from transformers import pipeline
    except Exception as e:
        raise ImportError("transformers not installed. Install it to use transformer summarization.") from e

    if model_name is None:
        model_name = "facebook/bart-large-cnn"

    # Build a simple chunker to handle long texts
    sentences = split_sentences(text)
    chunk_size_chars = 4000  # approximate chunk size
    chunks = []
    cur = ""
    for s in sentences:
        if len(cur) + len(s) + 1 > chunk_size_chars and cur:
            chunks.append(cur.strip())
            cur = s + " "
        else:
            cur += s + " "
    if cur:
        chunks.append(cur.strip())

    summarizer = pipeline("summarization", model=model_name)

    summary_parts = []
    for chunk in chunks:
        # Ensure non-empty
        if not chunk.strip():
            continue
        try:
            # The model may require min_length/max_length; adapt reasonably
            summary = summarizer(chunk, max_length=max_length, min_length=40)
            if isinstance(summary, list) and len(summary) > 0:
                summary_parts.append(summary[0]['summary_text'])
            else:
                summary_parts.append(str(summary))
        except Exception:
            # If a chunk fails, skip it
            continue

    if not summary_parts:
        return text  # Fallback to full text
    return ' '.join(summary_parts)

# -----------------------------
# Article extraction helpers
# -----------------------------
def extract_title(soup):
    # Try Open Graph first, then title tag, then h1
    og_title = soup.find('meta', property='og:title')
    if og_title and og_title.get('content'):
        return og_title['content'].strip()
    if soup.title and soup.title.string:
        return soup.title.string.strip()
    h1 = soup.find('h1')
    if h1 and h1.get_text(strip=True):
        return h1.get_text(strip=True)
    return None

def extract_date(soup):
    # Common meta fields
    meta_props = [
        ('meta', {'property': 'article:published_time'}),
        ('meta', {'property': 'og:published_time'}),
        ('meta', {'name': 'pubdate'}),
        ('meta', {'name': 'PublishDate'}),
        ('time', {}),
    ]
    for tag, attrs in meta_props:
        el = soup.find(tag, attrs=attrs)
        if el:
            content = el.get('content') or el.get_text(strip=True)
            if content:
                return content.strip()
    # Fallback: look for time tag
    t = soup.find('time')
    if t and t.get('datetime'):
        return t['datetime']
    return None

def extract_text_from_article(soup):
    # Try common article containers
    article = soup.find('article')
    text_parts = []
    if article:
        for p in article.find_all('p'):
            s = p.get_text(strip=True)
            if len(s) > 40:
                text_parts.append(s)
    # If not found, try other containers
    if not text_parts:
        candidates = [
            {'tag': 'div', 'attrs': {'class': re.compile(r'(article|article-content|article-body|post-content|content)')}},
            {'tag': 'section', 'attrs': {'class': re.compile(r'(article|article-content|article-body|post-content|content)')}},
        ]
        for c in candidates:
            container = soup.find(c['tag'], attrs=c['attrs'])
            if container:
                for p in container.find_all('p'):
                    s = p.get_text(strip=True)
                    if len(s) > 40:
                        text_parts.append(s)
            if text_parts:
                break
    # Final fallback: all paragraphs in page
    if not text_parts:
        for p in soup.find_all('p'):
            s = p.get_text(strip=True)
            if len(s) > 40:
                text_parts.append(s)

    return '\n'.join(text_parts).strip()

# -----------------------------
# Main scraper
# -----------------------------
def scrape_news(start_url, max_articles=10, article_link_selector=None, max_delay=2.0, 
                summarize_method='extractive', summary_sentences=3, transformers_model=None,
                output_file='scraped_news.json'):
    headers = {
        'User-Agent': 'NewsScraper/1.0 (+https://example.com/bot)'
    }

    session = requests.Session()
    session.headers.update(headers)

    try:
        resp = session.get(start_url, timeout=15)
        resp.raise_for_status()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Failed to fetch start URL: {start_url}\nError: {e}")
        return

    soup = BeautifulSoup(resp.text, 'html.parser')

    # Gather article URLs
    article_urls = []
    if article_link_selector:
        for a in soup.select(article_link_selector):
            href = a.get('href')
            if not href:
                continue
            full = urljoin(start_url, href)
            if full not in article_urls:
                article_urls.append(full)
    else:
        # Fallback heuristic: collect all hrefs that look like article URLs
        for a in soup.find_all('a', href=True):
            href = a['href']
            full = urljoin(start_url, href)
            if full in article_urls:
                continue
            # Heuristics: domain same as start_url and contains common article cues
            if url_in_domain(full, start_url) and ('/news/' in full or '/article' in full or '/story' in full or '/202' in full or '/health' in full):
                article_urls.append(full)

    if not article_urls:
        print("No article URLs found. Consider providing a valid article link selector.")
        return

    results = []
    count = 0
    for url in article_urls:
        if count >= max_articles:
            break

        try:
            r = session.get(url, timeout=15)
            r.raise_for_status()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Failed to fetch article: {url}\nError: {e}")
            continue

        a_soup = BeautifulSoup(r.text, 'html.parser')
        title = extract_title(a_soup) or "Untitled"
        date = extract_date(a_soup)

        content_text = extract_text_from_article(a_soup)
        if not content_text:
            content_text = ""
        # Prepare summary
        summary = ""
        text_for_summary = content_text if content_text else title

        if text_for_summary and summarize_method:
            if summarize_method.lower() == 'extractive':
                summary = summarize_extractive(text_for_summary, max_sentences=summary_sentences)
            elif summarize_method.lower() in ('transformer', 'auto'):
                try:
                    summary = summarize_transformer(text_for_summary, max_length=summary_sentences*50, model_name=transformers_model)
                except Exception as e:
                    # Fallback to extractive if transformer fails
                    summary = summarize_extractive(text_for_summary, max_sentences=summary_sentences)
            else:
                summary = text_for_summary
        else:
            summary = text_for_summary

        article_data = {
            'url': url,
            'title': title,
            'date': date,
            'content': content_text,
            'summary': summary
        }
        results.append(article_data)

        count += 1
        # Polite delay
        time.sleep(random.uniform(0.6, 1.6))

    # Write output
    if results:
        with open(output_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            json.dump(results, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
        print(f"Saved {len(results)} articles to {output_file}")
    else:
        print("No articles scraped.")

# Helper: check domain match
def url_in_domain(target, base_url):
    try:
        base = re.sub(r'^https?://', '', base_url).rstrip('/')
        t = re.sub(r'^https?://', '', target).rstrip('/')
        return base in t or base.split('/')[0] in t
    except Exception:
        return False

# -----------------------------
# Example usage
# -----------------------------
if __name__ == '__main__':
    # User should customize:
    # - start_url: landing page or sitemap with article links
    # - article_link_selector: CSS selector for article links on the landing page (optional)
    # - max_articles: how many articles to process
    # - summarize_method: 'extractive' or 'transformer' (requires transformers)
    # - summary_sentences: number of sentences in the summary (for extractive)
    #
    # Example (pseudo):
    # start_url = "https://www.example-news-site.com/"
    # article_link_selector = "a.card__title"  # adjust to site
    # scrape_news(start_url, max_articles=5, article_link_selector=article_link_selector,
    #             summarize_method='extractive', summary_sentences=3, output_file='news.json')
    #
    # Below is a placeholder you should replace with real site details.

    # ---- Replace with real site details to run ----
    start_url = "https://www.example-news-site.com/"
    article_link_selector = None  # e.g., 'a.article-link' if you have one
    max_articles = 6
    summarize_method = 'extractive'  # or 'transformer'
    summary_sentences = 4
    transformers_model = None  # e.g., 'facebook/bart-large-cnn' if you want to force a model

    # Call the scraper
    scrape_news(
        start_url=start_url,
        max_articles=max_articles,
        article_link_selector=article_link_selector,
        max_delay=2.0,
        summarize_method=summarize_method,
        summary_sentences=summary_sentences,
        transformers_model=transformers_model,
        output_file='scraped_news.json'
    )
```

How to adapt to a specific site:
- Identify how article links are structured on the site. If there’s a listing page, supply a CSS selector that targets the article link anchors (for example: "a.headline-link" or "div.news-item a").
- If you don’t provide a selector, the script will try to collect candidate links heuristically (same domain and containing common article path hints).
- You may need to tweak extract_text_from_article to target the site’s article container (e.g., class names like article-content, post-content, entry-content, etc.).

Notes and tips:
- If you want to use transformer-based summarization, install transformers (pip install transformers) and ensure you have access to a compatible model. Large models may require a GPU and can be slow.
- The extractive summarizer is lightweight and works without extra dependencies.
- Respect robots.txt and the site’s terms of service. If a site blocks scraping, stop and consider alternative access methods like RSS/Atom feeds or official APIs.
- If you want to extend, you can add:
  - RSS/Atom feed parsing for easier article discovery.
  - Rate limiting, caching, or saving intermediate results to avoid re-scraping.
  - Output in CSV, SQLite, or Pandas DataFrame for analytics.

Here’s a concise way to think about it:

- How memories form: We don’t store a literal recording of events. Encoding depends on what caught our attention, how emotionally salient something was, our prior knowledge, and expectations. What we later recall is a reconstruction, not a rewind.

- Why emotions matter: Strong emotions (especially fear or stress) can enhance memory for central details but can distort peripheral details. The amygdala can modulate how the hippocampus encodes memories, making some parts vivid while others fade or become distorted.

- The reconstructive retrieval process: When we remember, we reconstruct the past using cues, current mood, and language. This reconstruction can introduce errors, especially if we’re exposed to misleading information after the event (misinformation effect), or if we imagine or tell ourselves stories about what happened (imagination inflation).

- Memory isn’t all-or-nothing: Some details may be accurate (the gist, order of major events, or recurring themes). Other details tend to be unreliable (exact times, sensory specifics, who said what).

- Common biases and errors:
  - Source misattribution: confusing where a memory came from (real event vs. a dream, a rumor, or a suggestion).
  - Confidence doesn’t guarantee accuracy: people can be highly confident about incorrect memories.
  - Consistency biases: we sometimes “remember” details to fit a current view of ourselves or the outcome.

- What research shows:
  - Eyewitness studies: people can be confidently wrong after misleading questions or exposure to incorrect information.
  - Recalling retrivals: repeatedly recalling or imagining an event can alter the memory itself (reconsolidation).
  - Flashbulb memories are vivid but not perfectly accurate; vividness isn’t a guarantee of truth.

- When this matters (practical takeaways):
  - For important memories (like eyewitness accounts), interviewers should avoid leading questions, encourage free recall, and seek corroboration from independent sources.
  - Be cautious about over-trusting your own memories, especially after discussing them with others or after emotional events.
  - Consider keeping notes or records of events when accuracy is critical.

- Why justice can be universal (the universalist case)

  - Impartiality and due process: The idea that people should be treated as equals in moral and legal regard, and that procedures should be fair, has wide appeal and can be defended as a condition for legitimate cooperation.
  - Philosophical theories: Some frameworks (e.g., Rawls’s justice as fairness, certain human-rights projects) try to ground justice in universal reasons that any reasonable person could endorse behind a veil of ignorance or from the standpoint of equal moral status.
  - Practical convergence: International law and human-rights norms attempt to articulate universal standards (e.g., protection from torture, basic rights to life and liberty) that transcend any single culture.

- Why justice is also context-bound (cultural and historical variation)
  - Different communities prioritize different values: equality, desert, need, solidarity, or duty, which affects distributive justice (how goods are shared) and retributive vs restorative justice (how wrongs are addressed).
  - Variations in institutions and norms: Family structures, property regimes, concepts of the self, and religious or philosophical traditions shape what counts as just, who counts as a moral considerandum, and what counts as an appropriate punishment or remedy.
  - Content and interpretation differ: Even when there is broad agreement that harm should be avoided, the specifics—who is owed what, how compensations are determined, what procedures are legitimate—vary across cultures and legal systems.

- How to think about it (a practical stance)
  - A hybrid view: Accept a baseline of universal commitments (e.g., dignity, non-arbitrary harm, basic rights) while allowing substantial, legitimate variation in how those commitments are interpreted and applied in different contexts.
  - Use cross-cultural justification: When proposing a principle, try to justify it in ways that others from different backgrounds can reasonably accept, aiming for impartial reasons rather than force or tradition alone.
  - Distinguish levels of justice: 
    - Interpersonal justice (fair treatment in everyday interactions)
    - Procedural justice (fair processes)
    - Distributive justice (fair allocation of goods and burdens)
    These can exhibit universal aspirations (fair treatment and due process) even as their concrete content varies region by region.
  - Be mindful of power dynamics: Claims to universality can become instruments of cultural dominance if not carefully debated. Dialogue and justification in public reasoned discourse help keep universality credible and legitimate.

It creates a heightmap, then maps elevations to an RGB terrain image (water, sand, grass, rocks, snow). It uses multi-octave Perlin noise for a natural look and a simple color blend to render terrain.

Requirements:
- numpy
- pillow
- noise

Install:
pip install numpy pillow noise

Code:

```python
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

# Perlin noise library (needs 'noise')
try:
    import noise
except ImportError:
    raise SystemExit("Missing 'noise' package. Install with: pip install noise")

def generate_heightmap(width, height, scale=0.04, octaves=6, persistence=0.5, lacunarity=2.0, seed=0):
    """
    Generate a 2D heightmap using multi-octave Perlin noise.

    - width, height: dimensions of the map
    - scale: frequency of the noise (smaller = larger features)
    - octaves, persistence, lacunarity: fractal brownian motion parameters
    - seed: integer seed for reproducibility (passed as 'base' to pnoise2)
    """
    hmap = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.float32)

    for y in range(height):
        ny = y / height
        for x in range(width):
            nx = x / width
            # Perlin noise value in [-1, 1]
            v = noise.pnoise2(nx * scale,
                              ny * scale,
                              octaves=octaves,
                              persistence=persistence,
                              lacunarity=lacunarity,
                              repeatx=1024,
                              repeaty=1024,
                              base=seed)
            hmap[y, x] = v

    # Normalize to [0, 1]
    min_v, max_v = hmap.min(), hmap.max()
    if max_v > min_v:
        hmap = (hmap - min_v) / (max_v - min_v)
    else:
        hmap.fill(0.0)
    return hmap

def height_to_color(hmap):
    """
    Map a heightmap (0..1) to an RGB image using terrain-like colors.

    - Deep water -> shallow water -> sand -> grass -> rock -> snow
    """
    h = np.clip(hmap, 0.0, 1.0)
    height, width = h.shape
    colors = np.zeros((height, width, 3), dtype=np.float32)

    # Color stops (RGB 0..1)
    deep_water = np.array([0.05, 0.10, 0.35])
    shallow_water = np.array([0.00, 0.40, 0.80])
    sand = np.array([0.76, 0.70, 0.50])
    grass = np.array([0.15, 0.55, 0.15])
    rock = np.array([0.50, 0.50, 0.50])
    snow = np.array([1.00, 1.00, 1.00])

    # 1) deep to shallow water
    m1 = h < 0.35
    t1 = h[m1] / 0.35  # 0..1
    colors[m1] = deep_water * (1 - t1[:, None]) + shallow_water * t1[:, None]

    # 2) sand (beach)
    m2 = (h >= 0.35) & (h < 0.60)
    t2 = (h[m2] - 0.35) / 0.25
    colors[m2] = shallow_water * (1 - t2[:, None]) + sand * t2[:, None]

    # 3) grasslands
    m3 = (h >= 0.60) & (h < 0.85)
    t3 = (h[m3] - 0.60) / 0.25
    colors[m3] = sand * (1 - t3[:, None]) + grass * t3[:, None]

    # 4) mountains / rocks
    m4 = h >= 0.85
    t4 = (h[m4] - 0.85) / 0.15
    colors[m4] = grass * (1 - t4[:, None]) + rock * t4[:, None]

    # Tiny snow cap at the very top
    colors[m4] = colors[m4] * 0.9 + snow * 0.1

    return colors

def save_terrain_image(heightmap, filename="terrain.png"):
    colors = height_to_color(heightmap)
    img = Image.fromarray((colors * 255).astype(np.uint8), mode="RGB")
    img.save(filename)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Parameters (tweak for different looks)
    width, height = 512, 512
    scale = 0.04        # smaller -> larger features
    octaves = 6
    persistence = 0.5
    lacunarity = 2.0
    seed = 42

    # Generate heightmap
    hmap = generate_heightmap(width, height, scale=scale, octaves=octaves,
                              persistence=persistence, lacunarity=lacunarity, seed=seed)

    # Save as an image (terrain.png)
    save_terrain_image(hmap, "terrain.png")
    print("Terrain generated and saved to terrain.png")
```

Notes and tips:
- The noise library’s pnoise2 supports octaves, persistence, and lacunarity, which gives a natural feel with relatively little code.
- You can experiment with parameters (scale, octaves, persistence, lacunarity, seed) to push the terrain toward mountains, plateaus, or broad plains.
- If you want even more realism, you can add:
  - A low-frequency “continent” mask to bias elevations to landmasses.
  - Erosion or hydraulic erosion steps (smoothing, river carving) after the heightmap is generated.
  - A 3D visualization (e.g., via matplotlib’s 3D plotting) to inspect the terrain mesh.

If you’d like, I can tailor the code to a specific size, color style, or add features like rivers or erosion-based refinement.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
  <title>Hide on Scroll Navbar</title>
  <style>
    /* Base styles */
    :root {
      --bg: #111;
      --fg: #fff;
    }
    * { box-sizing: border-box; }
    body {
      margin: 0;
      font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Arial;
      background: #f4f4f4;
      color: #333;
    }

    /* Fixed header with smooth hide/show */
    .site-header {
      position: fixed;
      top: 0; left: 0; right: 0;
      z-index: 999;
      transform: translateY(0);
      transition: transform 0.3s ease-in-out;
      will-change: transform;
    }

    .nav {
      display: flex;
      align-items: center;
      justify-content: space-between;
      padding: 14px 20px;
      background: rgba(17, 17, 17, 0.95);
      color: #fff;
      min-height: 60px;
      border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08);
      backdrop-filter: saturate(1.2) blur(2px);
    }

    .logo {
      font-weight: 700;
      letter-spacing: .5px;
    }

    /* Desktop menu */
    .menu {
      display: flex;
      gap: 1rem;
      list-style: none;
      padding: 0; margin: 0;
    }
    .menu a {
      color: #fff;
      text-decoration: none;
      padding: 8px 12px;
      border-radius: 6px;
    }
    .menu a:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.1); }

    /* Mobile: hamburger button */
    .hamburger {
      display: none;
      width: 40px; height: 32px;
      border: none;
      background: transparent;
      cursor: pointer;
      padding: 0;
      color: #fff;
      flex-direction: column;
      justify-content: center;
      gap: 6px;
    }
    .hamburger span {
      display: block;
      height: 3px; width: 100%;
      background: #fff; border-radius: 2px;
    }

    /* Hide header when scrolling down */
    .nav-hidden {
      transform: translateY(-100%);
    }

    /* Mobile menu behavior */
    @media (max-width: 768px) {
      .hamburger { display: flex; }
      .menu {
        position: absolute;
        top: 60px;
        left: 0;
        right: 0;
        flex-direction: column;
        background: rgba(17,17,17,0.95);
        overflow: hidden;
        max-height: 0;
        transition: max-height 0.3s ease;
      }
      .menu.open { max-height: 420px; } /* enough to show items */
      .menu a { padding: 12px 20px; }
    }

    /* Page content to enable scrolling */
    main {
      padding: 100px 20px; /* leave space for fixed header */
      max-width: 900px;
      margin: 0 auto;
    }
    section {
      height: 700px;
      background: #fff;
      border: 1px solid #ddd;
      border-radius: 8px;
      padding: 20px;
      margin-bottom: 40px;
      box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.05);
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <header class="site-header" id="header" aria-label="Site header">
    <nav class="nav">
      <div class="logo">Brand</div>

      <button class="hamburger" id="hamburger" aria-label="Toggle menu" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="navMenu">
        <span></span><span></span><span></span>
      </button>

      <ul class="menu" id="navMenu">
        <li><a href="#home">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="#features">Features</a></li>
        <li><a href="#pricing">Pricing</a></li>
        <li><a href="#contact">Contact</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </header>

  <main>
    <section id="home"><h2>Home</h2><p>Scroll to see the navbar hide on scroll down and reappear on scroll up.</p></section>
    <section id="features"><h2>Features</h2><p>More content to enable scrolling...</p></section>
    <section id="pricing"><h2>Pricing</h2><p>More content to enable scrolling...</p></section>
    <section id="contact"><h2>Contact</h2><p>More content to enable scrolling...</p></section>
  </main>

  <script>
    // Hide on scroll down, show on scroll up
    (function() {
      const header = document.getElementById('header');
      let lastScrollY = window.scrollY;
      let ticking = false;

      function onScroll() {
        const current = window.scrollY;

        // If scrolling down past the header height, hide
        if (current > lastScrollY && current > header.offsetHeight) {
          header.classList.add('nav-hidden');
        } else {
          header.classList.remove('nav-hidden');
        }

        lastScrollY = current;
        ticking = false;
      }

      window.addEventListener('scroll', function() {
        if (!ticking) {
          window.requestAnimationFrame(onScroll);
          ticking = true;
        }
      });

      // Mobile menu toggle
      const hamburger = document.getElementById('hamburger');
      const navMenu = document.getElementById('navMenu');

      hamburger.addEventListener('click', function() {
        const isOpen = navMenu.classList.toggle('open');
        hamburger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(isOpen));
      });

      // Close mobile menu when a link is clicked
      navMenu.querySelectorAll('a').forEach(a => {
        a.addEventListener('click', () => {
          if (navMenu.classList.contains('open')) {
            navMenu.classList.remove('open');
            hamburger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
          }
        });
      });
    })();
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

How it works
- The header uses position: fixed so it stays at the top, with a transform that slides it out of view when hidden.
- JavaScript tracks scroll direction. If you scroll down, it adds the nav-hidden class; if you scroll up, it removes it.
- A simple responsive menu (hamburger) appears on small screens. Toggling it opens/closes the vertical menu.

Let's finalize the code block for the single HTML file:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Drag & Drop To-Do List</title>
  <style>
    .container { max-width: 900px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 20px; }
    .lists { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 20px; }
    .list { border: 1px solid #ddd; padding: 10px; min-height: 200px; border-radius: 8px; background: #fdfdfd; }
    ul.task-list { padding: 0; margin: 0; min-height: 180px; }
    .task { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; padding: 8px 10px; margin: 6px 0; border: 1px solid #ddd; border-radius: 4px; background: #fff; cursor: grab; }
    .task.done { text-decoration: line-through; color: #888; background: #f3f3f3; }
    .task .delete { border: none; background: transparent; color: #888; cursor: pointer; font-size: 14px; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container">
    <div class="header">
      <h1>Drag & Drop To-Do List</h1>
    </div>
    <div class="input-area">
       <input id="taskInput" placeholder="Add a new task..." />
       <button id="addBtn">Add</button>
    </div>
    <div class="lists">
       <section>
         <h2>To Do</h2>
         <ul id="todoList" class="task-list" data-list="todo"></ul>
       </section>
       <section>
         <h2>Done</h2>
         <ul id="doneList" class="task-list" data-list="done"></ul>
       </section>
    </div>
    <button id="clearAll">Clear All</button>
  </div>

  <script>
    const STORAGE_KEY = 'todo-app-v1';
    let tasks = [];

    function generateId() {
      return 'id_' + Date.now().toString(36) + '_' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 6);
    }

    function save() {
      localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(tasks));
    }

    function load() {
      const s = localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
      tasks = s ? JSON.parse(s) : [];
    }

    function normalizeAllOrders() {
      const todo = tasks.filter(t => !t.completed).sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order);
      todo.forEach((t, idx) => t.order = idx + 1);
      const done = tasks.filter(t => t.completed).sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order);
      done.forEach((t, idx) => t.order = idx + 1);
      save();
    }

    function render() {
      const todoList = document.getElementById('todoList');
      const doneList = document.getElementById('doneList');
      todoList.innerHTML = '';
      doneList.innerHTML = '';

      tasks.forEach(t => {
        const li = createLi(t);
        if (t.completed) {
          doneList.appendChild(li);
        } else {
          todoList.appendChild(li);
        }
      });
    }

    function createLi(task) {
      const li = document.createElement('li');
      li.className = 'task' + (task.completed ? ' done' : '');
      li.draggable = true;
      li.dataset.id = task.id;
      li.innerHTML = `<span class="task-text">${escapeHTML(task.text)}</span><button class="delete" aria-label="Delete task">✕</button>`;
      
      li.addEventListener('dragstart', e => {
        e.dataTransfer.setData('text/plain', JSON.stringify({ id: task.id }));
        e.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = 'move';
      });

      li.addEventListener('dblclick', () => editTask(task, li));
      li.querySelector('.delete').addEventListener('click', () => {
          tasks = tasks.filter(x => x.id !== task.id);
          normalizeAllOrders();
          render();
      });

      return li;
    }

    function editTask(t, li) {
      const current = t.text;
      li.innerHTML = `<input class="edit" value="${escapeHTML(current)}" />`;
      const input = li.querySelector('input');
      input.focus();
      input.select();

      input.addEventListener('blur', () => {
        const val = input.value.trim();
        if (val.length > 0) t.text = val;
        render();
      });
      input.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === 'Escape') {
          render();
        }
      });
    }

    function escapeHTML(s) {
      const div = document.createElement('div');
      div.textContent = s;
      return div.innerHTML;
    }

    document.getElementById('addBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
      const input = document.getElementById('taskInput');
      const text = input.value.trim();
      if (!text) return;

      const last = tasks.filter(t => !t.completed).sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order).pop();
      const order = last ? last.order + 1 : 1;
      const newTask = { id: generateId(), text, completed: false, order };
      tasks.push(newTask);
      input.value = '';
      normalizeAllOrders();
      render();
    });

    document.getElementById('taskInput').addEventListener('keydown', e => {
      if (e.key === 'Enter') document.getElementById('addBtn').click();
    });

    document.getElementById('clearAll').addEventListener('click', () => {
      if (confirm('Clear all tasks?')) {
        tasks = [];
        localStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY);
        render();
      }
    });

    load();
    render();
    window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', render);
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

To run this application, simply copy and paste the provided code into a new HTML file named `index.html` and open it in a web browser! You can add tasks, drag to reorder, and clear the list as needed.</think> Here's a complete, self-contained HTML file for a drag-and-drop to-do list with localStorage support. It includes:

- Add tasks
- Drag tasks between "To Do" and "Done"
- Reorder tasks by dragging one task before another
- Delete tasks
- Inline editing (double-click a task to edit)
- Local storage persistence

Copy this into an index.html file and open in a browser.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <title>Drag & Drop To-Do List with Local Storage</title>
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
  <style>
    :root {
      --bg: #f6f7fb;
      --card: #ffffff;
      --border: #e3e5e8;
      --text: #1f2937;
      --muted: #6b7280;
      --todo: #e8f0fe;
      --done: #e6ffe6;
    }

    * { box-sizing: border-box; }
    html, body { height: 100%; }
    body {
      margin: 0;
      font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Arial;
      background: var(--bg);
      color: var(--text);
    }

    .container {
      max-width: 1100px;
      margin: 40px auto;
      padding: 0 20px;
    }

    header {
      display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center;
      gap: 16px; padding: 6px 0 18px;
    }
    h1 { font-size: 1.4rem; margin: 0; }

    .input-row {
      display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center;
      margin-bottom: 14px;
    }
    #taskInput {
      flex: 1; padding: 12px 14px; font-size: 1rem;
      border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 6px;
      background: #fff;
    }
    #addBtn {
      padding: 12px 16px; font-size: 1rem;
      border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 6px;
      background: #4f46e5; color: #fff; cursor: pointer;
    }
    #addBtn:hover { background: #4338ca; }

    .lists {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
      gap: 16px;
      align-items: start;
    }

    .panel {
      background: #fff;
      border: 1px solid var(--border);
      border-radius: 8px;
      padding: 12px;
      min-height: 260px;
    }

    .panel h2 {
      font-size: 1.05rem;
      margin: 0 0 8px 6px;
      color: #374151;
    }

    .task-list {
      list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0;
      min-height: 180px;
    }

    .task {
      display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center;
      padding: 8px 10px; margin: 6px 0;
      border: 1px solid var(--border);
      border-radius: 6px;
      background: #fff;
      cursor: grab;
    }
    .task.done {
      text-decoration: line-through;
      color: var(--muted);
      background: #f3f4f6;
    }
    .task .task-text {
      flex: 1; padding: 0 6px;
    }
    .task .delete {
      border: none; background: transparent; color: #888;
      cursor: pointer; font-size: 14px; padding: 4px 8px; border-radius: 4px;
    }
    .task .delete:hover { color: #e11d48; }

    /* Empty state hints (optional) */
    .hint {
      color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.92rem; padding: 8px 6px;
    }

    /* Responsive tweaks */
    @media (max-width: 800px) {
      .lists { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container">
    <header>
      <h1>Drag & Drop To-Do</h1>
    </header>

    <div class="input-row" aria-label="Add new task">
      <input id="taskInput" placeholder="Add a new task and press Enter" />
      <button id="addBtn" aria-label="Add task">Add</button>
    </div>

    <div class="lists">
      <section class="panel" aria-label="To Do list">
        <h2>To Do</h2>
        <ul id="todoList" class="task-list" data-list="todo"></ul>
      </section>

      <section class="panel" aria-label="Done list">
        <h2>Done</h2>
        <ul id="doneList" class="task-list" data-list="done"></ul>
      </section>
    </div>

    <div style="margin-top:14px;">
      <button id="clearAll" class="secondary" aria-label="Clear all tasks">Clear All</button>
    </div>
  </div>

  <script>
    (function() {
      const STORAGE_KEY = 'todo-app-v1';
      let tasks = [];

      function generateId() {
        return 'id_' + Date.now().toString(36) + '_' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 6);
      }

      function escapeHTML(s) {
        const d = document.createElement('div');
        d.textContent = s;
        return d.innerHTML;
      }

      function save() {
        localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(tasks));
      }

      function load() {
        const s = localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
        if (s) {
          try {
            tasks = JSON.parse(s);
          } catch (e) {
            tasks = [];
          }
        } else {
          tasks = [];
        }
      }

      function normalizeAllOrders() {
        const todo = tasks.filter(t => !t.completed).sort((a,b)=> a.order - b.order);
        todo.forEach((t, idx) => t.order = idx + 1);
        const done = tasks.filter(t => t.completed).sort((a,b)=> a.order - b.order);
        done.forEach((t, idx) => t.order = idx + 1);
        save();
      }

      function render() {
        const todoList = document.getElementById('todoList');
        const doneList = document.getElementById('doneList');
        todoList.innerHTML = '';
        doneList.innerHTML = '';

        const todo = tasks.filter(t => !t.completed).sort((a,b)=> a.order - b.order);
        const done = tasks.filter(t => t.completed).sort((a,b)=> a.order - b.order);

        function createLi(task) {
          const li = document.createElement('li');
          li.className = 'task';
          if (task.completed) li.classList.add('done');
          li.draggable = true;
          li.dataset.id = task.id;
          li.innerHTML = `<span class="task-text">${escapeHTML(task.text)}</span>
                          <button class="delete" aria-label="Delete task">✕</button>`;

          li.addEventListener('dragstart', (e) => {
            e.dataTransfer.setData('text/plain', JSON.stringify({ id: task.id }));
            e.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = 'move';
          });

          li.addEventListener('dragover', (e) => e.preventDefault());

          li.addEventListener('drop', (e) => {
            e.preventDefault();
            const payload = JSON.parse(e.dataTransfer.getData('text/plain') || '{}');
            if (!payload.id) return;
            const dragged = tasks.find(x => x.id === payload.id);
            if (!dragged) return;
            if (dragged.id === task.id) return;

            // Insert dragged before the target task within the same list
            dragged.completed = (task.completed);
            // Build the target list
            let list = tasks.filter(x => x.completed === dragged.completed).sort((a,b)=> a.order - b.order);
            // Remove dragged from that list if present
            const idxDrag = list.findIndex(x => x.id === dragged.id);
            if (idxDrag !== -1) list.splice(idxDrag, 1);
            // Insert before the target
            const idxTarget = list.findIndex(x => x.id === task.id);
            if (idxTarget === -1) {
              list.push(dragged);
            } else {
              list.splice(idxTarget, 0, dragged);
            }
            // Update orders in that list
            list.forEach((it, i) => it.order = i + 1);
            // Reflect changes back to global tasks
            list.forEach(it => {
              const t = tasks.find(x => x.id === it.id);
              if (t) {
                t.order = it.order;
                t.completed = it.completed;
              }
            });
            normalizeAllOrders();
            render();
          });

          // Delete button
          li.querySelector('.delete').addEventListener('click', () => {
            tasks = tasks.filter(x => x.id !== task.id);
            normalizeAllOrders();
            render();
          });

          // Edit on dbl-click
          li.addEventListener('dblclick', () => editTask(task, li));

          return li;
        }

        function addToList(container, t) {
          container.appendChild(createLi(t));
        }

        todo.forEach(t => addToList(todoList, t));
        done.forEach(t => addToList(doneList, t));

        // Allow dropping onto lists to append to end
        [todoList, doneList].forEach(listEl => {
          listEl.addEventListener('dragover', (e) => e.preventDefault());

          listEl.addEventListener('drop', (e) => {
            e.preventDefault();
            const payload = JSON.parse(e.dataTransfer.getData('text/plain') || '{}');
            if (!payload.id) return;
            const dragged = tasks.find(x => x.id === payload.id);
            if (!dragged) return;

            const targetListKey = listEl.dataset.list; // 'todo' or 'done'
            dragged.completed = (targetListKey === 'done');
            // Build the target list for dragged.completed
            let list = tasks.filter(x => x.completed === dragged.completed).sort((a,b)=> a.order - b.order);
            // Remove dragged from that list if present
            const idxDrag = list.findIndex(x => x.id === dragged.id);
            if (idxDrag !== -1) list.splice(idxDrag, 1);
            // Move to end of that list
            list.push(dragged);
            list.forEach((it, i) => it.order = i + 1);
            list.forEach(it => {
              const t = tasks.find(x => x.id === it.id);
              if (t) { t.order = it.order; t.completed = it.completed; }
            });
            normalizeAllOrders();
            render();
          });
        });
      }

      function editTask(t, li) {
        const current = t.text;
        li.innerHTML = `<input class="edit" value="${escapeHTML(current)}" />`;
        const input = li.querySelector('input');
        input.focus();
        input.select();
        function commit() {
          const val = input.value.trim();
          if (val.length > 0) t.text = val;
          render();
        }
        input.addEventListener('blur', commit);
        input.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
          if (e.key === 'Enter') commit();
          if (e.key === 'Escape') render();
        });
      }

      function initDatasetListAttributes() {
        document.getElementById('todoList').dataset.list = 'todo';
        document.getElementById('doneList').dataset.list = 'done';
      }

      // UI handlers
      document.getElementById('addBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
        const input = document.getElementById('taskInput');
        const text = input.value.trim();
        if (!text) return;
        // Determine end order for To Do
        const last = tasks.filter(t => !t.completed).sort((a,b)=> a.order - b.order).pop();
        const order = last ? last.order + 1 : 1;
        const newTask = { id: generateId(), text, completed: false, order };
        tasks.push(newTask);
        input.value = '';
        normalizeAllOrders();
        render();
      });

      document.getElementById('taskInput').addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
        if (e.key === 'Enter') document.getElementById('addBtn').click();
      });

      document.getElementById('clearAll').addEventListener('click', () => {
        if (confirm('Clear all tasks?')) {
          tasks = [];
          localStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY);
          render();
        }
      });

      function init() {
        load();
        // Ensure lists exist (for data attributes)
        initDatasetListAttributes();
        // Normalize any missing orders
        tasks.forEach((t, idx) => {
          if (typeof t.order !== 'number' || t.order < 1) t.order = idx + 1;
        });
        render();
      }

      // Start
      window.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init);
    })();
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

How it works (brief):
- Tasks are stored in localStorage under the key todo-app-v1.
- You can add tasks with the input and Add button (or press Enter).
- Drag a task to another list (To Do or Done) to move it between states. You can also drag a task onto another task to insert before it.
- Dragging between lists reorders items and keeps two separate sequences: one for To Do and one for Done.
- Double-click a task to edit it inline.
- Delete a task with the X button.
- Clear All removes everything (with a confirmation).

If you want a single-page app without server dependencies, this approach provides a robust, client-side solution with drag-and-drop and persistence.

Here's the complete code!</think> Here's a self-contained Python script that detects anomalies in time-series data using Isolation Forest. It converts the time-series into window-based features (mean, std, min, max, slope, and the last value in the window) and then fits an Isolation Forest on the training portion. It outputs anomaly labels for each window and can optionally plot the results.

Save as detect_anomalies_iforest.py and run with Python 3.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Anomaly detection in time-series using Isolation Forest.

What it does:
- Reads a CSV with at least two columns: a timestamp and a value.
- Converts the time-series into window-based features:
  - mean, std, min, max, slope (linear trend in the window), and last_value.
- Splits data into training (assumed normal) and testing portions.
- Trains an Isolation Forest on the training portion.
- Predicts anomalies for all windows.
- Optional: plots the series and marks detected anomalies.

Usage (example):
  python detect_anomalies_iforest.py --input data.csv --time-col timestamp --value-col value --window 30 --train-ratio 0.7 --contamination 0.01 --n-estimators 200 --plot
"""

import argparse
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import sys

def create_window_features(series, times, window_size):
    """
    Build window-based features for a univariate time-series.

    Returns:
      X: numpy array of shape (n_windows, 6) -> [mean, std, min, max, slope, last_value]
      out_times: numpy array of timestamps corresponding to the end of each window
      last_values: numpy array of the last value in each window (same as series[end_index])
    """
    n = len(series)
    if window_size < 2:
        raise ValueError("window_size must be at least 2 to compute slope.")
    if n < window_size:
        raise ValueError("Not enough data points for the specified window size.")

    X = []
    out_times = []
    last_values = []

    for i in range(window_size - 1, n):
        window = series[i - window_size + 1: i + 1]
        mean = float(np.mean(window))
        std = float(np.std(window, ddof=1)) if window_size > 1 else 0.0
        mn = float(np.min(window))
        mx = float(np.max(window))
        # Slope via linear fit: fit to indices 0..window_size-1
        x = np.arange(window_size)
        slope = float(np.polyfit(x, window, 1)[0])
        last = float(series[i])

        X.append([mean, std, mn, mx, slope, last])
        out_times.append(times[i])
        last_values.append(last)

    return np.array(X), np.array(out_times), np.array(last_values)

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Anomaly detection in time-series using Isolation Forest.")
    parser.add_argument("--input", required=True, help="Path to CSV file containing the time-series data.")
    parser.add_argument("--time-col", default="timestamp", help="Name of the timestamp column.")
    parser.add_argument("--value-col", default="value", help="Name of the value column.")
    parser.add_argument("--window", type=int, default=30, help="Window size for feature extraction.")
    parser.add_argument("--train-ratio", type=float, default=0.7, help="Proportion of data used for training (normal data).")
    parser.add_argument("--contamination", type=float, default=0.01, help="Expected fraction of anomalies (for Isolation Forest).")
    parser.add_argument("--n-estimators", type=int, default=200, help="Number of trees in the forest.")
    parser.add_argument("--max-samples", default="auto", help="Number of samples to draw to train each tree.")
    parser.add_argument("--random-state", type=int, default=42, help="Random seed.")
    parser.add_argument("--output", default=None, help="Path to save the results CSV (optional).")
    parser.add_argument("--plot", action="store_true", help="Plot the time-series with anomalies highlighted.")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    # Load data
    df = pd.read_csv(args.input)
    if args.time_col not in df.columns or args.value_col not in df.columns:
        print(f"Error: CSV must contain columns '{args.time_col}' and '{args.value_col}'.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    # Parse time column
    try:
        df[args.time_col] = pd.to_datetime(df[args.time_col])
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error parsing time column: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    # Sort by time
    df = df.sort_values(by=args.time_col).reset_index(drop=True)

    times = df[args.time_col].values
    values = df[args.value_col].astype(float).values

    # Create features
    try:
        X, feature_times, last_values = create_window_features(values, times, args.window)
    except ValueError as ve:
        print(f"Error: {ve}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    if X.shape[0] == 0:
        print("No windows were generated. Check the window size and data length.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    # Determine train/test split
    n_windows = X.shape[0]
    train_size = int(n_windows * args.train_ratio)
    if train_size < 1:
        print("Training size too small. Increase data or adjust train_ratio.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    X_train = X[:train_size]
    X_all = X  # keep for predictions on all windows

    # Train Isolation Forest
    clf = IsolationForest(
        n_estimators=args.n_estimators,
        max_samples=args.max_samples,
        contamination=args.contamination,
        random_state=args.random_state
    )
    clf.fit(X_train)

    # Predict on all windows
    preds = clf.predict(X_all)  # 1 normal, -1 anomaly
    anomaly_flags = preds == -1

    # Build results
    results = pd.DataFrame({
        "timestamp": feature_times,
        "window_end_value": last_values,
        "value": last_values,  # same as window end value
        "mean": X_all[:, 0],
        "std": X_all[:, 1],
        "min": X_all[:, 2],
        "max": X_all[:, 3],
        "slope": X_all[:, 4],
        "anomaly": anomaly_flags
    })

    # Save results if requested
    if args.output:
        results.to_csv(args.output, index=False)
        print(f"Results saved to {args.output}")

    # Optional plotting
    if args.plot:
        # Plot the original series
        plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
        plt.plot(feature_times, last_values, label="Window end value", alpha=0.7)
        # Mark anomalies
        anomaly_times = results.loc[results["anomaly"], "timestamp"]
        anomaly_vals = results.loc[results["anomaly"], "window_end_value"]
        plt.scatter(anomaly_times, anomaly_vals, color="red", marker="x", s=80, label="Anomaly")
        plt.xlabel("Time")
        plt.ylabel("Value")
        plt.title("Time-series with Anomalies Detected by Isolation Forest")
        plt.legend()
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Notes and tips:
- The script treats the time-series as a sequence of windows. Each window yields a feature vector: [mean, std, min, max, slope, last_value].
- It assumes most of the data is normal (hence train_ratio default 0.7). If you have labeled normal data, you can adjust accordingly.
- Contamination is a hint to the model about the expected fraction of anomalies; adjust via --contamination.
- For multivariate time-series, you can extend the feature set to include more variables per window (e.g., separate features for each variable).
- If you don’t want to plot, skip --plot. If you want to save results, supply --output.

If you’d like, I can tailor the script to your data format or provide a version that uses lag features instead of window statistics.

I'll present everything clearly in a code block for the user.</think> Here's a self-contained Python example that uses a genetic algorithm to optimize a Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) route. It includes:

- City generation (random coordinates)
- Distance matrix
- GA with elitism, tournament selection, order crossover (OX), and swap mutation
- Optional plotting (if matplotlib is available)

Copy and run as-is.

```python
import random
import math
from typing import List, Tuple

# City representation: (x, y)
City = Tuple[float, float]
Route = List[int]


def generate_cities(n: int, seed: int | None = None) -> List[City]:
    if seed is not None:
        random.seed(seed)
    return [(random.uniform(0, 100), random.uniform(0, 100)) for _ in range(n)]


def distance(a: City, b: City) -> float:
    dx = a[0] - b[0]
    dy = a[1] - b[1]
    return math.hypot(dx, dy)


def compute_distance_matrix(cities: List[City]) -> List[List[float]]:
    n = len(cities)
    dist = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(n):
            dist[i][j] = distance(cities[i], cities[j])
    return dist


def route_distance(route: Route, dist: List[List[float]]) -> float:
    total = 0.0
    n = len(route)
    for i in range(n):
        a = route[i]
        b = route[(i + 1) % n]
        total += dist[a][b]
    return total


def route_fitness(route: Route, dist: List[List[float]]) -> float:
    # Higher fitness for shorter routes
    return 1.0 / route_distance(route, dist)


def random_route(n: int) -> Route:
    r = list(range(n))
    random.shuffle(r)
    return r


def initialize_population(pop_size: int, n: int) -> List[Route]:
    return [random_route(n) for _ in range(pop_size)]


def ox_crossover(parent1: Route, parent2: Route) -> Route:
    """Order Crossover (OX1)"""
    n = len(parent1)
    a = random.randrange(n)
    b = random.randrange(a, n)

    child = [None] * n
    # Copy segment from parent1
    for i in range(a, b + 1):
        child[i] = parent1[i]

    # Fill remaining positions with order from parent2
    p2_idx = 0
    for i in range(n):
        idx = (b + 1 + i) % n
        if child[idx] is None:
            while parent2[p2_idx] in child:
                p2_idx += 1
            child[idx] = parent2[p2_idx]
            p2_idx += 1

    return child


def swap_mutation(route: Route, mutation_rate: float) -> Route:
    r = route[:]
    n = len(r)
    for i in range(n):
        if random.random() < mutation_rate:
            j = random.randrange(n)
            r[i], r[j] = r[j], r[i]
    return r


def tournament_selection(pop: List[Route], dist: List[List[float]], tournament_size: int) -> Route:
    best = None
    best_fit = -1.0
    for _ in range(tournament_size):
        ind = random.randrange(len(pop))
        fit = route_fitness(pop[ind], dist)
        if best is None or fit > best_fit:
            best = pop[ind]
            best_fit = fit
    return best


def evolve_population(
    pop: List[Route],
    dist: List[List[float]],
    mutation_rate: float,
    elitism: int,
    tournament_size: int
) -> List[Route]:
    # Evaluate and sort by fitness (descending)
    scored = [(route, route_fitness(route, dist)) for route in pop]
    scored.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)

    new_pop: List[Route] = [s[0] for s in scored[:elitism]]  # elitism

    # Generate rest via crossover + mutation
    while len(new_pop) < len(pop):
        parent1 = tournament_selection(pop, dist, tournament_size)
        parent2 = tournament_selection(pop, dist, tournament_size)
        child = ox_crossover(parent1, parent2)
        child = swap_mutation(child, mutation_rate)
        new_pop.append(child)

    return new_pop


def plot_route(cities: List[City], route: Route, title: str = "TSP Route") -> None:
    try:
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

        xs = [cities[i][0] for i in route] + [cities[route[0]][0]]
        ys = [cities[i][1] for i in route] + [cities[route[0]][1]]
        plt.figure(figsize=(6, 6))
        plt.plot(xs, ys, '-o')
        plt.title(title)
        plt.axis('equal')
        plt.show()
    except Exception:
        # If plotting is not available, skip silently
        pass


def main():
    random.seed(42)

    # TSP parameters
    n_cities = 20
    pop_size = 100
    generations = 500
    mutation_rate = 0.02
    elitism = 5
    tournament_size = 5

    # Generate cities and distance matrix
    cities = generate_cities(n_cities, seed=123)
    dist = compute_distance_matrix(cities)

    # Initialize population
    population = initialize_population(pop_size, n_cities)

    best_route = None
    best_distance = float('inf')

    # Evolution loop
    for gen in range(generations):
        # Evaluate current best
        for route in population:
            d = route_distance(route, dist)
            if d < best_distance:
                best_distance = d
                best_route = route[:]

        population = evolve_population(
            population,
            dist,
            mutation_rate,
            elitism,
            tournament_size
        )

        # Optional: print progress every 50 generations
        if (gen + 1) % 50 == 0 or gen == 0:
            print(f"Generation {gen+1}: best distance = {best_distance:.4f}")

    # Final best
    final_distance = route_distance(best_route, dist)
    print("\nFinal best route distance:", final_distance)
    print("Best route (city indices):", best_route)

    # Optional: plot
    plot_route(cities, best_route, title=f"Best route (distance={final_distance:.2f})")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Notes:
- This is a straightforward GA for TSP with elitism, tournament selection, order crossover (OX1), and swap mutation.
- You can tweak parameters: population size, generations, mutation_rate, elitism, and tournament_size to trade off speed and solution quality.
- If you have matplotlib installed, the script will plot the final route. If not, it will skip plotting gracefully.

To ensure equal shares of a sum among four people, the total must ideally be divisible by 4. Here are the steps you can follow:

Method (generic)
- Let the total sum be T.
- Each equal share = T / 4.

Practical with currency
- If you can use decimals (dollars and cents) and T is divisible by 4, just give T/4 to each person.
- If you’re limited to the smallest currency unit (cents) and T is not divisible by 4:
  - Convert to cents: N = total in cents.
  - Base share per person: B = floor(N / 4) cents.
  - Remainder: R = N mod 4 (R is 0, 1, 2, or 3).
  - A fair approach is to give B cents to each person, then distribute the R extra cents one by one to R of the people. This makes those R shares one cent larger than the others, so it is not perfectly equal in cash terms.

  - Alternatively, acknowledge the limitation and use a ledger (IOUs or digital credits) to represent the exact equal share of T/4 for each person.

Example
- Total T = $52.31.
- Each person’s exact share = $52.31 / 4 = $13.0775.
- In cents: N = 5231.
  - B = floor(5231/4) = 1307 cents ($13.07).
  - R = 5231 mod 4 = 3.
  - Give three people $13.08 and one person $13.07. If you want strict long-term equality, hold the remaining 1 cent in reserve or wait until you can make the total divisible by 4.

Bottom line
- The equal share is T/4. Use that as the target. In real cash, handle any indivisible remainder with a fair policy (rounding with rotation, IOUs, or a reserve) to maintain long-term fairness.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
  <title>Live Character Counter</title>
  <style>
    :root {
      --bg: #f7f7fb;
      --card: #fff;
      --text: #1f2937;
      --muted: #6b7280;
      --green: #4caf50;
      --orange: #b45309;
      --red: #991b1b;
    }

    * { box-sizing: border-box; }

    body {
      margin: 0;
      font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Arial, sans-serif;
      background: var(--bg);
      color: var(--text);
    }

    .container {
      max-width: 680px;
      margin: 40px auto;
      padding: 22px;
      background: var(--card);
      border-radius: 12px;
      box-shadow: 0 6px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.06);
    }

    h1 {
      font-size: 1.4rem;
      margin: 0 0 6px;
    }

    p.lead {
      color: var(--muted);
      margin: 0 0 14px;
    }

    .field { display: block; }
    label { display: block; font-weight: 600; margin-bottom: 6px; }

    textarea {
      width: 100%;
      min-height: 120px;
      padding: 12px;
      font: inherit;
      border-radius: 8px;
      border: 1px solid #ddd;
      resize: vertical;
      outline: none;
    }

    .progress {
      height: 8px;
      background: #e5e7eb;
      border-radius: 6px;
      overflow: hidden;
      margin-top: 8px;
    }

    .progress > span {
      display: block;
      height: 100%;
      width: 0%;
      background: #4caf50;
      transition: width .15s ease-in-out;
    }

    .hint {
      margin-top: 8px;
      font-size: 14px;
      color: var(--muted);
      display: flex;
      gap: 12px;
      align-items: center;
      flex-wrap: wrap;
    }

    .counter { font-weight: 700; }

    /* Status colors for the counter text (optional visual cue) */
    .counter.ok { color: #374151; }
    .counter.warn { color: #b45309; }
    .counter.exceed { color: #991b1b; }

  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <main class="container" aria-label="Live character counter demo">
    <h1>Live Character Counter</h1>
    <p class="lead">Type in the textarea to see the character count update in real time. The maximum length is enforced by the input’s maxlength attribute.</p>

    <div class="field">
      <label for="textarea">Your text</label>
      <textarea id="textarea" maxlength="200" placeholder="Start typing…"></textarea>

      <div class="progress" aria-hidden="true">
        <span id="progressBar"></span>
      </div>

      <div class="hint" aria-live="polite">
        <span class="counter" id="charCount">0 / 200</span>
        <span id="charsLeft">200 characters left</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  </main>

  <script>
    (function () {
      const textarea = document.getElementById('textarea');
      const max = parseInt(textarea.getAttribute('maxlength'), 10) || 200;
      const bar = document.getElementById('progressBar');
      const countEl = document.getElementById('charCount');
      const leftEl = document.getElementById('charsLeft');

      function update() {
        const len = textarea.value.length;
        // Clamp just in case someone pastes beyond maxlength via alternate means
        const clamped = Math.min(len, max);
        const remaining = max - clamped;
        const percent = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, (clamped / max) * 100));

        // Update progress bar width and color
        bar.style.width = percent + '%';
        if (remaining <= 0) {
          bar.style.background = '#991b1b'; // red
        } else if (remaining <= Math.ceil(max * 0.25)) {
          bar.style.background = '#b45309'; // orange
        } else {
          bar.style.background = '#4caf50'; // green
        }

        // Update counter text and status
        countEl.textContent = `${clamped} / ${max}`;
        leftEl.textContent = remaining + ' characters left';
        countEl.classList.remove('ok', 'warn', 'exceed');
        if (remaining <= 0) countEl.classList.add('exceed');
        else if (remaining <= Math.ceil(max * 0.25)) countEl.classList.add('warn');
        else countEl.classList.add('ok');
      }

      textarea.addEventListener('input', update);
      update(); // initial state
    })();
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

How to customize
- Change the max length: adjust the maxlength attribute on the textarea (e.g., maxlength="500").
- Tailor visuals: tweak colors in CSS or adjust the threshold logic in JavaScript (the 25% remaining threshold is just a suggestion).

How the long-division process works (step by step)
- Start with the leftmost digits of the dividend (the 3-digit number) and see how many times the divisor goes into them.
- Write that count as the next digit of the quotient.
- Multiply the divisor by that digit, subtract from the current chunk to get a remainder.
- Bring down the next digit of the dividend to form a new chunk, and repeat.
- When you’ve used all digits, the quotient is what you’ve written, and the remainder is whatever is left (if any).

Two worked examples

1) 438 ÷ 6
- Look at the leftmost digits: 4 is less than 6, so take 43.
- How many times does 6 fit into 43? 7 times (7×6=42; 8×6=48 is too big). First quotient digit is 7.
- Subtract: 43 − 42 = 1.
- Bring down the next digit (the 8) to make 18.
- How many times does 6 fit into 18? 3 times (3×6=18). Subtract to get 0.
- No remainder, and the quotient digits are 7 and 3, so 438 ÷ 6 = 73.

2) 302 ÷ 7
- The first digit 3 is too small for 7, so take 30.
- How many times does 7 fit into 30? 4 times (4×7=28; 5×7=35 is too big). First quotient digit is 4.
- Subtract: 30 − 28 = 2.
- Bring down the next digit (the 2) to make 22.
- How many times does 7 fit into 22? 3 times (3×7=21; 4×7=28 too big). Subtract to get 1.
- Quotient digits are 4 and 3, so 302 ÷ 7 = 43 with remainder 1.

Tips for doing this without a calculator
- Use the multiples table (1×d, 2×d, …, 9×d) to estimate how many times d fits into the current chunk.
- If the leftmost digit is smaller than the divisor, combine it with the next digit (like turning 4 into 43 when dividing by 6).
- After each subtraction, always bring down the next digit to form a new chunk.
- Check your result by recomputing: divisor × quotient + remainder should equal the original number.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import math
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def sierpinski(ax, depth, p1, p2, p3):
    if depth == 0:
        ax.fill([p1[0], p2[0], p3[0]], [p1[1], p2[1], p3[1]], color='black', edgecolor='k')
    else:
        # midpoints
        m12 = ((p1[0]+p2[0])/2.0, (p1[1]+p2[1])/2.0)
        m23 = ((p2[0]+p3[0])/2.0, (p2[1]+p3[1])/2.0)
        m31 = ((p3[0]+p1[0])/2.0, (p3[1]+p1[1])/2.0)
        sierpinski(ax, depth-1, p1, m12, m31)
        sierpinski(ax, depth-1, m12, p2, m23)
        sierpinski(ax, depth-1, m31, m23, p3)

def koch_line(ax, depth, p1, p2):
    if depth == 0:
        ax.plot([p1[0], p2[0]], [p1[1], p2[1]], color='blue', linewidth=1)
    else:
        dx = (p2[0]-p1[0])/3.0
        dy = (p2[1]-p1[1])/3.0
        a = (p1[0]+dx, p1[1]+dy)
        c = (p1[0]+2*dx, p1[1]+2*dy)
        vx = c[0]-a[0]
        vy = c[1]-a[1]
        cos60 = 0.5
        sin60 = math.sqrt(3)/2.0
        b = (a[0] + cos60*vx - sin60*vy, a[1] + sin60*vx + cos60*vy)
        koch_line(ax, depth-1, p1, a)
        koch_line(ax, depth-1, a, b)
        koch_line(ax, depth-1, b, c)
        koch_line(ax, depth-1, c, p2)

def koch_snowflake(ax, depth, side_length=1.0):
    height = (math.sqrt(3)/2.0) * side_length
    p1 = (0.0, 0.0)
    p2 = (side_length, 0.0)
    p3 = (side_length/2.0, height)
    koch_line(ax, depth, p1, p2)
    koch_line(ax, depth, p2, p3)
    koch_line(ax, depth, p3, p1)

def cantor(ax, depth, x, y, length):
    if depth == 0:
        ax.plot([x, x+length], [y, y], color='black')
    else:
        l = length/3.0
        cantor(ax, depth-1, x, y, l)
        cantor(ax, depth-1, x+2*l, y, l)

def hilbert_curve(ax, order, size=1.0, color='green'):
    pts = []
    def rec(n, x, y, xi, xj, yi, yj):
        if n == 0:
            pts.append((x+xi, y+yi))
        else:
            rec(n-1, x, y, yi/2.0, yj/2.0, xi/2.0, xj/2.0)
            rec(n-1, x+xi/2.0, y+xj/2.0, xi/2.0, xj/2.0, yi/2.0, yj/2.0)
            rec(n-1, x+xi/2.0+yi/2.0, y+yj/2.0+xj/2.0, -xi/2.0, -xj/2.0, -yi/2.0, -yj/2.0)
            rec(n-1, x+yi/2.0, y+yj/2.0, -yi/2.0, -yj/2.0, -xi/2.0, -xj/2.0)
    rec(order, 0.0, 0.0, size, 0.0, 0.0, size)

def main():
    plt.figure(figsize=(10,10))
    gs = plt.GridSpec(2,2, wspace=0.3, hspace=0.3)

    ax0 = plt.subplot(gs[0,0])
    sierpinski(ax0, depth=5, p1=(0.0, 0.0), p2=(1.0, 0.0), p3=(0.5, math.sqrt(3)/2.0))
    ax0.set_aspect('equal')
    ax0.axis('off')
    ax0.set_title('Sierpinski triangle')

    ax1 = plt.subplot(gs[0,1])
    koch_snowflake(ax1, depth=4, side_length=1.0)
    ax1.set_aspect('equal')
    ax1.axis('off')
    ax1.set_title('Koch snowflake')

    ax2 = plt.subplot(gs[1,0])
    cantor(ax2, depth=4, x=0.0, y=0.0, length=1.0)
    ax2.set_xlim(-0.05, 1.05)
    ax2.set_ylim(-0.15, 0.15)
    ax2.axis('off')
    ax2.set_title('Cantor set (1D)')

    ax3 = plt.subplot(gs[1,1])
    hilbert_curve(ax3, order=5, size=1.0, color='orange')
    ax3.set_aspect('equal')
    ax3.axis('off')
    ax3.set_title('Hilbert curve (order 5)')

    plt.show()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```</think> Here's a self-contained Python script that visualizes several fractals using recursive algorithms. It uses matplotlib and provides four classic examples: Sierpinski triangle, Koch snowflake, Cantor set, and the Hilbert curve. You can adjust the recursion depths (or order) to see more/less detail.

Save as fractals_recursion.py and run with Python.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import math
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def sierpinski(ax, depth, p1, p2, p3):
    """
    Recursively draw a Sierpinski triangle.
    depth: recursion depth. depth==0 draws a filled triangle.
    p1, p2, p3: vertices of the triangle (tuples like (x, y))
    """
    if depth == 0:
        ax.fill([p1[0], p2[0], p3[0]],
                [p1[1], p2[1], p3[1]],
                color='black', edgecolor='black')
    else:
        m12 = ((p1[0] + p2[0]) / 2.0, (p1[1] + p2[1]) / 2.0)
        m23 = ((p2[0] + p3[0]) / 2.0, (p2[1] + p3[1]) / 2.0)
        m31 = ((p3[0] + p1[0]) / 2.0, (p3[1] + p1[1]) / 2.0)
        sierpinski(ax, depth - 1, p1, m12, m31)
        sierpinski(ax, depth - 1, m12, p2, m23)
        sierpinski(ax, depth - 1, m31, m23, p3)


def koch_line(ax, depth, p1, p2):
    """
    Recursively draw a Koch curve segment from p1 to p2.
    depth==0 draws the line; otherwise subdivide into 4 segments with a peak.
    """
    if depth == 0:
        ax.plot([p1[0], p2[0]], [p1[1], p2[1]], color='blue', linewidth=1)
    else:
        dx = (p2[0] - p1[0]) / 3.0
        dy = (p2[1] - p1[1]) / 3.0
        a = (p1[0] + dx, p1[1] + dy)          # 1/3 point
        c = (p1[0] + 2 * dx, p1[1] + 2 * dy)  # 2/3 point

        # Peak of the equilateral bump on segment a--c
        vx = c[0] - a[0]
        vy = c[1] - a[1]
        cos60 = 0.5
        sin60 = math.sqrt(3) / 2.0
        b = (a[0] + cos60 * vx - sin60 * vy,
             a[1] + sin60 * vx + cos60 * vy)

        koch_line(ax, depth - 1, p1, a)
        koch_line(ax, depth - 1, a, b)
        koch_line(ax, depth - 1, b, c)
        koch_line(ax, depth - 1, c, p2)


def koch_snowflake(ax, depth, side_length=1.0):
    """
    Draw a Koch snowflake by applying Koch line to the three sides
    of an equilateral triangle.
    """
    height = (math.sqrt(3) / 2.0) * side_length
    p1 = (0.0, 0.0)
    p2 = (side_length, 0.0)
    p3 = (side_length / 2.0, height)

    koch_line(ax, depth, p1, p2)
    koch_line(ax, depth, p2, p3)
    koch_line(ax, depth, p3, p1)


def cantor(ax, depth, x, y, length):
    """
    Recursively draw Cantor set on a horizontal line y.
    depth: recursion depth. depth==0 draws a single segment of given length.
    """
    if depth == 0:
        ax.plot([x, x + length], [y, y], color='black')
    else:
        l = length / 3.0
        cantor(ax, depth - 1, x, y, l)
        cantor(ax, depth - 1, x + 2 * l, y, l)


def hilbert_curve(ax, order, size=1.0, color='green'):
    """
    Draw the Hilbert curve of given order using a recursive algorithm.
    The curve is built in a 0..size square.
    """
    pts = []

    def rec(n, x, y, xi, xj, yi, yj):
        if n == 0:
            # Append the end point of this small segment
            pts.append((x + xi, y + yi))
        else:
            rec(n - 1, x, y, yi / 2.0, yj / 2.0, xi / 2.0, xj / 2.0)
            rec(n - 1, x + xi / 2.0, y + xj / 2.0, xi / 2.0, xj / 2.0,
                yi / 2.0, yj / 2.0)
            rec(n - 1, x + xi / 2.0 + yi / 2.0, y + yj / 2.0 + xj / 2.0,
                -xi / 2.0, -xj / 2.0, -yi / 2.0, -yj / 2.0)
            rec(n - 1, x + yi / 2.0, y + yj / 2.0,
                -yi / 2.0, -yj / 2.0, -xi / 2.0, -xj / 2.0)

    # Start in a size x size square
    rec(order, 0.0, 0.0, size, 0.0, 0.0, size)

    xs, ys = zip(*pts)
    ax.plot(xs, ys, color=color, linewidth=1)


def main():
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 10))
    gs = plt.GridSpec(2, 2, wspace=0.3, hspace=0.3)

    # Sierpinski triangle
    ax0 = plt.subplot(gs[0, 0])
    p1 = (0.0, 0.0)
    p2 = (1.0, 0.0)
    p3 = (0.5, math.sqrt(3) / 2.0)
    sierpinski(ax0, depth=5, p1=p1, p2=p2, p3=p3)
    ax0.set_aspect('equal')
    ax0.axis('off')
    ax0.set_title('Sierpinski triangle')

    # Koch snowflake
    ax1 = plt.subplot(gs[0, 1])
    koch_snowflake(ax1, depth=4, side_length=1.0)
    ax1.set_aspect('equal')
    ax1.axis('off')
    ax1.set_title('Koch snowflake')

    # Cantor set
    ax2 = plt.subplot(gs[1, 0])
    cantor(ax2, depth=4, x=0.0, y=0.0, length=1.0)
    ax2.set_xlim(-0.05, 1.05)
    ax2.set_ylim(-0.15, 0.15)
    ax2.axis('off')
    ax2.set_title('Cantor set (1D)')

    # Hilbert curve
    ax3 = plt.subplot(gs[1, 1])
    hilbert_curve(ax3, order=5, size=1.0, color='orange')
    ax3.set_aspect('equal')
    ax3.axis('off')
    ax3.set_title('Hilbert curve (order 5)')

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

Notes:
- You can adjust the recursion depths (depth for Sierpinski, Koch, Cantor; order for Hilbert) to control the complexity.
- The script draws four subplots in one window. You can modify the depths/order or plot each fractal separately as you prefer.

  <script>
    // Real-time clock with dynamic greeting based on the time of day.
    (function () {
      const timeEl = document.getElementById('time');
      const dateEl = document.getElementById('date');
      const greetingEl = document.getElementById('greeting');
      const emojiEl = document.getElementById('icon'); // optional, not used here
      const toggleBtn = document.getElementById('toggleFormat');
      const srFormat = document.getElementById('sr-format');

      // 12h by default; store preference in localStorage
      let is24Hour = false;
      const saved = localStorage.getItem('clock24');
      if (saved !== null) {
        is24Hour = saved === 'true';
      }

      function update() {
        const now = new Date();
        const hour24 = now.getHours();
        const minute = now.getMinutes();
        const second = now.getSeconds();

        // Greeting based on 0-23 hours
        let greeting;
        if (hour24 < 6) {
          greeting = 'Good night';
        } else if (hour24 < 12) {
          greeting = 'Good morning';
        } else if (hour24 < 18) {
          greeting = 'Good afternoon';
        } else {
          greeting = 'Good evening';
        }

        // Emoji indicator based on time
        let emoji;
        if (hour24 < 6 || hour24 >= 22) {
          emoji = '🌙';
        } else if (hour24 < 12) {
          emoji = '☀️';
        } else if (hour24 < 18) {
          emoji = '🌤️';
        } else {
          emoji = '🌆';
        }

        // Time formatting
        let h = hour24;
        let ampm = '';
        if (!is24Hour) {
          ampm = h >= 12 ? 'PM' : 'AM';
          h = h % 12;
          if (h === 0) h = 12;
        }

        const hh = String(h).padStart(2, '0');
        const mm = String(minute).padStart(2, '0');
        const ss = String(second).padStart(2, '0');
        const timeString = is24Hour
          ? `${hh}:${mm}:${ss}`
          : `${hh}:${mm}:${ss} ${ampm}`;

        // Update DOM
        timeEl.textContent = timeString;
        dateEl.textContent = now.toLocaleDateString(undefined, {
          weekday: 'long',
          year: 'numeric',
          month: 'long',
          day: 'numeric'
        });
        greetingEl.textContent = `${greeting} ${emoji}`;

        // Optional: update sr-only text for accessibility
        srFormat.textContent = is24Hour
          ? 'Clock is in 24-hour format.'
          : 'Clock is in 12-hour format.';
        toggleBtn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(is24Hour));

        // Optional: subtle background change over day
        // (Not required for functionality; can be extended)
      }

      // Toggle between 12h and 24h
      toggleBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
        is24Hour = !is24Hour;
        localStorage.setItem('clock24', String(is24Hour));
        // Update button label to reflect new mode
        toggleBtn.textContent = is24Hour
          ? 'Switch to 12-hour'
          : 'Switch to 24-hour';
        update();
      });

      // Initialize button label based on current mode
      toggleBtn.textContent = is24Hour ? 'Switch to 12-hour' : 'Switch to 24-hour';
      // Initial update
      update();
      // Update every second
      setInterval(update, 1000);
    })();
  </script>
</body>
</html>

Notes:
- The clock updates every second and shows a dynamic greeting: Good night (0–5), Good morning (6–11), Good afternoon (12–17), Good evening (18–23).
- You can switch between 12-hour and 24-hour formats. The preference is saved in localStorage.
- The layout is responsive and includes a decorative icon and a date display. You can customize colors or add more styling as needed.
